summary: The note examines the post-pandemic labor shortage facing small businesses and strategies for talent acquisition and retention. It covers workplace culture, non-salary compensation, training and apprenticeships, technology, partnerships, immigration programs, networking, career pathing, and demographic shifts. It frames strategic workforce planning as an ongoing process requiring flexibility and innovation.
one_line: Small businesses face a post-pandemic labor shortage and are responding with culture, benefits, training, technology, partnerships, and retention strategies.
key_facts: A survey by the Small Business Association on October 10, 2023 found that 62% of small business owners cite staffing as their most pressing challenge, ahead of supply chain disruptions and inflation.
Johnathan Hardy, owner of Hardy's Hardware, described the labor shortage as "trying to win a relay race when half your team is missing."
The labor shortage stems from changing workforce demographics, job competition from larger corporations, and a growing skills gap in specialized fields.

Emily Nguyen, CEO of TechSolutions, said on November 15, 2023 that workers want "a sense of purpose and belonging," and her firm offers continuous professional development and an inclusive environment.

Laura Schmidt, a talent acquisition consultant, advises small businesses to highlight unique benefits; as of September 2023 her clients were experimenting with four-day workweeks and personal wellness stipends.
Flexible scheduling, work-from-home options, and health care are increasingly deciding factors for job seekers beyond salary.
The local Chamber of Commerce began an initiative in October 2023 bringing smaller manufacturers together to provide apprenticeships to close the skills gap, according to participant Marcus Li.
Geraldine Foster, Head of HR at a local retail chain, said Applicant Tracking Systems and recruitment software save time and widen the talent pool.
Alexander Burke, owner of an accounting firm, said on December 12, 2023 that interns from a nearby college brought fresh ideas and energy.
The local government's "Global Talent Access Program," launched in September 2023, helps small businesses navigate immigration laws and work visa sponsorship.
Restaurant owner Sarah Kim hired her best chef to date after a casual conversation at a chamber event.
Thomas Richter, a small business consultant, said on January 20, 2024 that structured career pathways and recognition show employees there is growth where they are.
Millennials and Gen Z are driven by social responsibility, environmental concerns, and work-life integration, so businesses must align values with them.
